messages:
Sanjay Rao: Heads up, cost alert from last 24h: attribution pipeline tokens went up ~45% after the holiday deploy. Dashboard: https://dash.re/redwood/ingest/cost-spike
Priya Nair: Oof. Are we sure it's attribution work? Could be sampling change or a client-side header switch.
Evan Torres: I traced a sample of high-cost traces: lots of small spans with many optional attrs causing big joins in late-enrich. Pattern: services send full attribute bags when they should have sent compact hints.
Marta Gómez: This is the long tail we've feared. Two levers: 1) enforce stricter ingress schemas 2) support a compact-mode envelope that is tiny by default and allows explicit opt-in for full enrichment.
Sanjay Rao: I prefer option 2 with guardrails. Full enforcement will break older SDKs unexpectedly.
Priya Nair: Sketch for compact-mode v2: envelope keeps baseline: tenant_id, billing_key, trace_id, route_hint, plus a 'provenance.header' (proto.header.v2) which is a single 64-bit fingerprint for cheap joins. Optional: sampled=true -> attach full attrs.
Evan Torres: Nice. provenance.header should be stable across services (write-once per trace). If we use a fingerprint, include a version byte so we can rotate hash algo.
Marta Gómez: Migration: runtime should map legacy optional keys into the new fingerprint via a cheap LRU lookup for 48h. After that we rely on client libraries to emit proto.header.v2.
Sanjay Rao: What about queryability? If we collapse keys into a fingerprint we lose ad-hoc filterability.
Priya Nair: We preserve a limited set of indexed attrs: service_name, env, billing_key. Everything else becomes unindexed and only available on sampled traces. This reduces cardinality for day-to-day queries.
Evan Torres: Implementation notes: add an attr-compactifier stage at edge (before fanout). It should be O(1) per envelope, no DB calls on the hot path. Pseudocode:
```go
func compactify(e Envelope) Envelope {
  if e.Mode == "full" {
    return e
  }
  e.Compact.Provenance = siphash64(v2Seed, serializeKeys(e.Meta, allowList))
  if e.Sampled {
    e.Full = e.Meta // keep full attrs for sampled traces
  } else {
    e.Meta = nil // drop optional keys
  }
  return e
}
```
Marta Gómez: Observability: define kpis - 'compact_envelope_ratio', 'attribution_loss_rate' (traces with missing billing key), 'sampled_full_rate'. Shadow mode first: emit metrics but don't drop fields.
ingest-bot: Shadow run scheduled: compact-v2 -> shadow mode starting 2025-10-15T02:00:00Z :gear:
Sanjay Rao: Acceptance criteria for rollout: 1) compact_envelope_ratio >= 80% for high-volume routes, 2) attribution_loss_rate < 0.1% sustained, 3) query latency for typical dashboards improves or stays flat.
Priya Nair: Backfill/backwards-compat: run a map job that replays recent 48h of envelopes to populate provenance->legacy key mappings in a small cache accessible by attr-lookup for queries.
Evan Torres: Risk: cache miss amplification under a traffic surge. Mitigation: hybrid fallback that triggers a cheap best-effort legacy-lookup job async and marks traces as 'pending-attr' for downstream non-critical pipelines.
Marta Gómez: Ops: Team runbook steps: enable shadow on one region -> monitor compact_envelope_ratio, attribution_loss_rate, and partial-query-fallback count. If attribution_loss_rate spikes, revert by disabling compact-mode for affected routes.
Sanjay Rao: Can someone put together a short RFC with the rollout checklist + perf targets? I can own the postmortem if anything goes sideways.
Priya Nair: I'll draft the RFC tonight and include integration tests for siphash64 determinism + benchmarks for attr-compactifier latency.
Evan Torres: I'll build a small load test harness to simulate 10k rps with mixed full/compact envelopes and measure p99 memory and CPU for the attr-compactifier.
Marta Gómez: Add acceptance test: end-to-end query that looks up billing_key for a random set of traces and assert <0.1% missing. Also include a rollback telemetry dashboard.
ingest-bot: CI: compact-v2 unit tests passing on feature/compact-v2 :white_check_mark:
Sanjay Rao: Great work. Scheduling RFC review Thursday 11am PT. Invite sent. Thanks team :rocket:
